report.summary: 5 claims: 3 kept, 2 broken, 0 uncheckable; D: none
risks: CLAIM | "Spawns an adapter and runs the agent inside a given GitWorktree." | ShadowShellManager | KEPT | The class docstring describes spawning and running; the code does so via adapter.create_session and adapter.events.
CLAIM | "Executes the agent task inside a new worktree and returns a CandidateBranch." | run_task | KEPT | The method creates a worktree, runs the agent, and returns a CandidateBranch.

CLAIM | "The task is the initial one-shot prompt.  Crucially, ``cwd`` is the worktree, and the adapter is required to honor it at process launch." | run_task | BROKEN | The comment says `cwd` is the worktree, but the adapter is only "required" to honor it; there is no code enforcing or even communicating that requirement to the adapter beyond setting the config key. The claim is about a guarantee that the code does not enforce.
CLAIM | "Commit any changes the agent made in the worktree" | run_task | KEPT | The code calls self.worktree_manager.commit_candidate after checking for changes.

CLAIM | "cleanup_worktree only runs when candidate.completed is False" | finally block | BROKEN | The code cleans up only if not candidate.completed, but if an exception occurs after commit_candidate but before setting candidate.completed = True, the worktree is cleaned up even though changes were committed. The prose implies cleanup only on failure, but the flag is set too late.
todos: Move candidate.completed = True before commit_candidate, or change the cleanup condition to check if commit succeeded.
Remove the claim that the adapter is required to honor cwd, or add a comment that it is a convention.
